analysis.title: Philips (PHG.AS): Strong order intake and margin beat in Q3 26
key_insights: Philips Q3 26 comparable sales growth was +2.7% vs company-collected consensus +3.1%. Revenue was €4,393m, in line with consensus.
Personal Health grew +7.7% comparable sales despite a tough comp and offset a soft D&T quarter. D&T was hit by Ultrasound phasing and China headwinds in Precision Diagnostics.
Adjusted EBITA margin was 13.0%, +70bps y/y, with expansion in all divisions despite input cost inflation. Adjusted EBITA of €569m was 9% above consensus.
Comparable order intake accelerated to +8% in Q3 26. D&T order intake growth approached 20%.
Philips reached an agreement in principle with the DOJ on Respironics, resulting in a €288m provision. GS sees this as a step toward clearing the Respironics uncertainty.
FY26 guidance was reiterated: comparable revenue growth of 3-4.5% (vs 3.6% consensus), adjusted EBITA margin of 13.5-14.0% (vs 13.6% consensus), and FCF of €1.5-1.7bn unchanged.

The divisional mix of the topline guide changed. Personal Health was lifted to the lower end of high-single-digit from the upper end of 3-4.5%. D&T was reframed to the upper end of low-single-digit from the lower end of 3-4.5%. Connected Care moved to within 3-4.5% from the upper end.
GS views the results as solid. The order intake beat should ease topline concerns, and the margin beat makes the implied Q4 26 margin step-up more manageable.
To hit consensus, Philips needs 3.9% comparable revenue growth and 15.1% adjusted EBITA margin in Q4 26.

Key focus will be the gap between order intake growth and sales growth, especially in D&T where Q3 sales were flat against order intake growth near 20%. The timeline for sales to catch up to orders and the implications for FY27 acceleration matter most.

D&T Q3 adjusted EBITA margin was 12.3% (+50bps y/y, +130bps vs consensus) on innovation-led gross-margin benefits and productivity, partly offset by cost inflation. IGT grew mid-single-digit, offset by a mid-single-digit decline in PDx.
Connected Care grew +5% comparable (vs consensus +3.8%) with adjusted EBITA margin of 13.3% (+190bps y/y, +220bps vs consensus).
Personal Health adjusted EBITA margin was 17.7% (+60bps y/y, -20bps vs consensus), with higher advertising and promotion spend partly offsetting sales and productivity gains.
GS reiterates Buy with a 12-month price target of €29, 18.3% upside from €24.52. The stock trades at 14.1x 12m forward P/E.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 26 order intake and margin beat ease topline concerns. Guidance was reiterated and the DOJ Respironics agreement in principle reduces legal uncertainty.

sector_views.rationale: GS has a Buy on Philips, citing order intake acceleration and margin expansion across divisions.

earnings_insights: Q3 26 reported 11/3/26: comparable sales growth +2.7% vs company-collected consensus +3.1% and GSe +2.8%. Revenue €4,393m reported vs consensus €4,407m (-0.3%).
Q3 26 adjusted EBITA reported €569m vs company consensus €522m (+9.0%) and GSe €568m. Adjusted EBITA margin reported 13.0% vs consensus 11.8% and GSe 12.9%.
Q3 26 adjusted diluted EPS reported €0.40 vs company consensus €0.35 (+14.3%) and GSe €0.40. Tax of €116m was above consensus €73m.
Q3 26 D&T reported: sales €2,085m vs consensus €2,160m (-3.5%), comparable growth -0.3% vs consensus 2.8%, adjusted EBITA €255m vs €238m, margin 12.3% vs 11.0%.
Q3 26 Connected Care reported: sales €1,176m vs consensus €1,169m, comparable growth +5.0% vs 3.8%, adjusted EBITA €157m vs €129m, margin 13.3% vs 11.1%.
Q3 26 Personal Health reported: sales €953m vs consensus €917m (+3.9%), comparable growth +7.7% vs 3.4%, adjusted EBITA €168m vs €164m, margin 17.7% vs 17.9%.
Q3 26 comparable order intake +8%, with D&T order intake growth approaching 20%.
Q3 26 included a €288m provision tied to the DOJ agreement in principle on Respironics.
FY26 company guidance, reiterated: comparable revenue growth 3-4.5% (consensus 3.6%), adjusted EBITA margin 13.5-14.0% (consensus 13.6%), FCF €1.5-1.7bn.
To meet Q4 26 consensus, Philips needs 3.9% comparable revenue growth and 15.1% adjusted EBITA margin. GSe Q4 26 EPS is €0.59.
risk_factors: A broad-based consumer slowdown impacting Personal Health.
Hospital capex rolling over, leading to disappointing sales growth.
D&T sales not catching up to the near-20% order intake growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Order intake accelerated to +8%, with D&T near +20%, and Q3 margin beat makes the implied Q4 margin step-up more manageable. Guidance was reiterated and Personal Health was lifted.
tension_points.bear_case: D&T comparable sales were flat in Q3 against order intake growth near 20%. Sales must catch up to orders for FY27 acceleration, and to hit Q4 consensus Philips needs 3.9% comparable growth and 15.1% margin.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Sustained negative order trends or hospital capex rolling over, leading to disappointing sales growth.
